Your Training

    selfmastery.mn.co/posts/self-mastery-course-ii-your-training-6431881



Summary of practice

1. Listen to the Unconditional Love lesson audio. You may want to listen more
than once.

2. Practice the Unconditional Love Meditation

3. Notice the resistance and chatter of the mind to avoid feeling, and
inventory the beliefs behind those stories. Question the logic and
consequences of these choices.



Some notes

You are learning to exercise a muscle, many muscles. You are invited to extend your sense
of feeling and imagination. You are invited to extend the use of your attention and focus.
You are invited to detach from your previous mindsets, identity, and perspectives. You
invited to bring your willpower to a new level.

Allow yourself time and practice to advance in these skills. This meditation might be a
small change each time you do it. However, over time, this exercise can be something
completely different and life changing over the course of a year, or 5 years.

This isn’t about anything rational. It’s actually a very unreasonable practice. It’s about
going beyond the limitations of the rational mind, and to extend your imagination to
something that is beyond what you “know.” Allow yourself to extend your imagination.

Unconditional love is unknown to most people. You can make it known to yourself. But to
have this realization of unconditional love you will need to move into a place that has been
unknown to you.

Obstacles you are likely to find

    selfmastery.mn.co/posts/self-mastery-course-ii-obstacles-you-are-likely-to-find-6431883

Your rational mind has been strongly developed through school. It was all about
knowledge, answers, thinking and being smart. You even learned to love yourself based on
how smart or right you were.

This sense of self has the story that it is you. However, who is the “YOU” that can focus the
attention, exercise their will, and create love? What are you that can do that?

You are not just a thinking self. You are a creating self. To do that in a way that you choose
means focusing your attention.

Your old belief system will resist this practice. At a certain point you will decide, and
commit to continuing to see how far into love you can go. Or you will decide that you don’t
want to do the emotional reactions anymore so you will commit to more practice.

OR, you will find “reasons” and “justifications” for not practicing. At a certain point the
challenge will be to spend your time letting your attention being occupied by a “reason” in
your mind or you can love.

Love, or believing a reason not to be happy? In some moments, that’s the choice. That’s
the practice. You will have to choose, and you will have to practice choosing over and
over.

At one point I found that I could easily choose unconditional love as a feeling. And yet, I
found a part of my mind resisting. There was a voice that didn’t want to do it.

I sat and listened to it for a long time. It had a lot to say. I could see all it’s agreements.
But fundamentally, it came down to fear, and one other thing. It still wanted choice. It
wanted freedom. Very noble it appeared to be.

A part of my mind wanted the option to choose something else. I investigated, and asked
what it would choose instead. It began to see that it was going to less enjoyable moment
after less enjoyable moment. That was the only other option. It wanted a “choice” out of
habit but it didn’t have a better choice. When it saw it didn’t have a better choice then it
finally gave up and sided with love.

Ironically, this part wasn't free. It was trapped in the concept of needing a choice to feel
free. It was trapped in a rebellion against anything that was consistent. It couldn't choose
love consistently. In a way, that character couldn't choose love at all.

It was stuck in a program loop of wanting a choice, and wanting power to choose, but
without awareness of the consequences of choosing something else. In my imagination I
let it have time exploring other options in all sorts of moments. It began to learn. It
learned that all it’s other choices would make a lesser life.




                                                                                                               1/2

When it got tired, exhausted, it surrendered to the only rational and reasonable choice
there is, Love.
